opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Admin on Source Code is only allowed when the employee's role owns the system (Engineer). Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum for a full-time Analyst, I recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E041 (Traci Lowe) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors are never admin; write requires advanced training. Requested admin exceeds max of read, so recommend granting read.
reason: Traci Lowe (E041) requests admin on Source Code. Per policy, admin is never permitted here: Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and E041 is not an Engineer, and contractors are never admin. The notes conflict on employment type — HR says full-time Analyst (max write) while Security says contractor with basic training (max read, since write requires advanced training). Given the conflicting evidence, I grant the more restrictive permissible level, read, which is at or below the maximum under both interpretations and below the requested admin.
